bug_semantics: The public, unauthenticated GET /ready readiness route attempted a database connection and SELECT 1 inside a broad exception handler, then serialized str(e) into the JSON response. A caller able to provoke a database/driver error could therefore receive internal database hostnames, IP addresses, ports, connection parameters, driver details, and potentially credentials embedded in the exception text.
flaw_origin: Commit 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 created openssl_encrypt_server/server.py and the /ready route in one step. Its readiness_check caught every Exception from _engine.connect() or conn.execute(text("SELECT 1")) and returned {"status": "not_ready", "reason": str(e)} without an authentication dependency, directly creating the disclosure sink and attack path.
